hero.lead: Twelve motifs from across Indonesia, sold by the metre. Width, weight, and region of origin are on every page — so you know exactly what is being cut.

featured.title: The ones people ask about most
featured.lead: The motifs visitors open most often, each with a macro view of the weave.

collections.title: Four ways cloth is made
collections.lead: Batik resists dye with wax, tenun builds the pattern from the threads themselves, songket floats a supplementary thread across the surface, and jumputan binds and stitches the cloth before dyeing.

anatomy.title: Reading the product details
anatomy.lead: Four numbers that decide whether a fabric suits your project.

width.desc: Measured in centimetres from selvedge to selvedge. It determines how many pattern pieces fit side by side, which directly changes the total metres you need to buy.

weight.desc: Grams per square metre. A low number means light and fluid; a high number means thicker and more structured. Shirts are usually comfortable between 120 and 160 gsm.

material.desc: Cotton breathes and is easy to care for. Silk is lighter with a natural sheen. Rayon drapes softly. Metallic thread adds shine but needs gentler handling.

technique.desc: This decides how the surface reads: wax resist produces crisp motif outlines, while ikat weaving gives the motif edges their characteristic feathering.

collections.title: Four techniques, four characters
collections.lead: How a cloth is made decides how it looks, how it hangs, and how it has to be cared for.
collections.ctaTitle: Not found what you are after?
collections.ctaLead: The full catalogue holds every motif, with filters for fibre, colour, and price.

blurb.batik: The motif is drawn in wax before the cloth is dyed, which gives batik its crisp outlines and layered colour. Usually on cotton — light and comfortable for everyday clothing.
blurb.tenun: The pattern is built from the threads during weaving rather than printed on the surface. The result is a reversible cloth with texture you can feel and motif edges you can recognise.
blurb.songket: A supplementary thread — often gold or silver — is laid in during weaving so the motif appears to float above the ground. These are the heaviest and most formal fabrics in the catalogue.
blurb.jumputan: The cloth is bound or stitched at chosen points before dyeing, so the gathered areas resist the colour and leave rippled patterns that are never quite identical twice.
